Rules for what a request keeps when its text does not fit

Source: R/core-context-policy.R
hr_context_policy.Rd

A context policy tells a packer, the code that fits named pieces of text into a request, what to do when they do not fit. pin names the pieces that are never cut, such as the question and the instructions. cut_order names the pieces cut first, in order; the pieces it does not name are cut after them, the last piece of the request first. keep says which part of a cut piece is kept (see hr_truncate()): one rule for every piece, or a character vector named by piece, with an unnamed element as the rule for the pieces it does not name. order_merges = TRUE asks the packers that merge findings to place them by the read's context_order as well; see gr_read_spec() for which packers those are.

Usage

hr_context_policy(
  pin = c("question", "instructions"),
  cut_order = character(0),
  keep = "head",
  order_merges = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'hr_context_policy'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

pin

Names of pieces that are never cut.

cut_order

Names of pieces cut first, in order.

keep

"head", "tail", "both" or "scored", or a character vector of them named by piece.

order_merges

Whether merge packers follow context_order.

x

An hr_context_policy.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class hr_context_policy: a list of pin, cut_order, keep and order_merges.

Details

A pinned piece is never cut by the policy. When the pinned pieces alone do not fit, hr_context_fit() says so (fits = FALSE) and leaves the decision to its caller.

hr_context_fit() applies a policy to a set of pieces. In the document layer, a read takes one as the context_policy setting of gr_read_spec(); NULL, the default, keeps each reader's own cuts.

See also

hr_context_fit(), hr_truncate(), gr_read_spec()

Other cost and token functions: hr_budget(), hr_context_fit(), hr_count_tokens(), hr_estimate_cost(), hr_load_models(), hr_model_info(), hr_model_limits(), hr_models(), hr_register_model(), hr_set_tokenizer(), hr_tokenizer(), hr_truncate(), hr_truncate_tokens()

Examples

p <- hr_context_policy(pin = c("question", "instructions", "draft"),
                       keep = c(excerpt = "both", "head"))
p
#> <hr_context_policy>
#>   pin:          question, instructions, draft
#>   cut first:    -
#>   keep:         excerpt = both, head
#>   order merges: FALSE
